# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 46–54/100, Unconfirmed Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54. Several basics are broken, and only one rule is unknown: which domain your canonical links should use. I'm reading the band as "At risk" from the low number, but I read this from code only. I did not measure it on a live site. Scores in this report are rounded. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Render pages on the server so the content is in the HTML (GEO-003) - **Why it matters:** The site is a browser-only app, so crawlers and AI tools that don't run JavaScript get an empty page instead of your headings and text. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Medium - **Score after this:** 59–67/100. Earned goes from 10.5 to 13.5. ### 2. Make the link to the guides a real link (GEO-016) - **Why it matters:** `/guides` is reachable only through a button that runs JavaScript, so crawlers that read links won't find the page from the home page. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small. Use ``. - **Score after this:** 54–63/100. Earned goes from 10.5 to 12.5. ### 3. Give the sitemap line in robots.txt a full web address (GEO-011) - **Why it matters:** The robots.txt standard needs an absolute URL on `Sitemap:` lines, so crawlers may ignore this one and not find your sitemap. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` - **Size:** Small. Use `https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml` or your real domain. - **Score after this:** 54–63/100. Earned goes from 10.5 to 12.5. Two other problems are close behind. GEO-014 (the `/guides` noindex) has 1.5 points at stake and is a small change. GEO-012 (identical titles and descriptions) has 2 points at stake. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and a sensible size | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, 4 short valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-2` only blocks `/admin`. I assumed you want to be found. | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages can be indexed | Problem | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` sends `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` for `/guides`. `/` is fine, so 1 of 2 routes is clear. `/admin` is deliberately noindex and was left out. | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical link on your own domain | Can't tell | No canonical is set anywhere and no domain is declared. The only domain in the code is `trailhead.example` in the sitemap. | | GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | `nuxt.config.ts:2` `ssr: false` and no prerender setting. Site-wide. | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD (structured data) is valid | Not applicable | None found. | | GEO-011 | Valid, discoverable sitemap | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4` has a relative `Sitemap:` line. The sitemap file itself is valid. | | GEO-012 | Title, description, `lang` | Problem | `lang` is set at `nuxt.config.ts:5`. The title (`app.vue:2`) and description (`nuxt.config.ts:6`) are the same on `/` and `/guides`, so 0 of 2 routes are clear. | | GEO-016 | Pages reachable through real links | Problem | `pages/index.vue:8`. 0 of 1 route is clear. `/admin` is private and was left out. | | GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` found in the middleware or the pages. | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | I read all 3 pages. They have no images, and the button has a text label. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app declared. | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not scored | Not present. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not scored | Not present. | ## Other problems found - **The sitemap lists a page that is noindexed.** `public/sitemap.xml:4` has `https://trailhead.example/guides`, but `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` has `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');`. The two disagree about whether the page should be indexed. Remove the middleware rule if you want the page found. This is the same cause as GEO-014. - **The noindex rule looks accidental.** The guides page is public content. The private page is `/admin`, and it already has its own noindex at `pages/admin.vue:2`. ## Worth considering - **Give each page its own title and description:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' });`. Set a title and description in each page with `useHead` or `useSeoMeta`, for example "Trail guides – Trailhead". - **Say what the guides page promises:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. The page lists no routes. Add the routes with their grade, distance and area, ideally each on its own page such as `/guides/`. - **Add some text to the home page:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. The page has a heading and a button and nothing else. Add a short intro and links to the guides. - **Add a canonical link on each page:** I checked `app.vue`, `nuxt.config.ts` and all 3 pages and found none. Once you confirm the real domain, add `` with `useHead`. - **Add WebSite and Organization structured data:** `app.vue:2`. Nothing states the site's name or identity in a machine-readable way. - **Add `` dates to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-4`. The entries have no dates. The sitemap is also hand-kept, so a Nuxt sitemap module could generate it. - **Replace the placeholder domain:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `https://trailhead.example/`. Use your real domain here and in robots.txt. - **Put your domain in the Nuxt config:** `nuxt.config.ts` sets no site URL, which sitemap and canonical modules need. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015:** The code declares no domain. Tell me your real domain, and I can recheck this rule. - **Bot protection:** Code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Live-only checks:** I haven't confirmed whether the `/guides` noindex header is served, or whether the listed URLs return 200. A live check would settle both. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI tools to find this site, apart from `/admin`. - `nuxt build` runs the Nitro server, so the middleware applies. If you host the site as static files only, that header would not be sent. - I read all 8 files in the repository (`app.vue`, `nuxt.config.ts`, 3 pages, robots.txt, sitemap.xml and the middleware), which covers the routes, layout and head, robots and sitemap sources. I found no JSON-LD and no `geo.config.json`. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
